unresolved: temporal-homes: the reference does not say that a hold in force stays in the entry file as one rule.
one-agent-default: the reference does not say one agent by default.

findings.summary: The check says that the reference tells where a hold in force goes: it stays in the entry file as one rule. The shipped reference has no such sentence. It lists "paused" as temporal text that is misplaced and gives only a log or the backlog as a home. The brief (one-pass, "Nothing temporal ...") says the hold stays in the entry file as one present-tense line, with its date and reason in the decision log. joycraft-prototype commit 83beff3 removed the row that said this.

The check says that the reference states one agent by default. The shipped reference always splits the pass into parts and gives each part its own agent, in parallel where the host has subagents; it never says that one agent is the default. Step 6 (lines 174-175) needs "an agent that wrote no edit" and gives no rule for a host with no subagents. Commit 83beff3 removed "One agent does it." The brief does not withdraw the panel ruling "One agent by default" by name; if the method of the best trial replaces it, the check needs an amendment by the owner, as one-pass-steps got.

Commit 83beff3 changed the reference and its tests together and removed assertions that two checks still need: the hold row from [AC:temporal-homes] (lines 114-123) and /One agent does it/ from [AC:one-agent-default] (lines 159-162). Both tests are green and each asserts less than its check says.

The check says that the skill says the full pass "runs on the owner's request and states its size first". The size statement is in the reference, not in SKILL.md, and applies only "above about 20,000 words of pages". The skill says "A person asks", not "the owner".
findings.assumption: The skill and the reference that it reads first count as one text, and a size statement for a large set only meets the check: the text for which the check was written (c586d0d) had the same condition, and step 1 always lists each page with its size.

findings.summary: The check says that the reference and setup.md say that a record is an audit trail. Only the reference uses those words (cleanup.md:90). setup.md says that a log is a record with a "search when ..." row and that no row tells an agent to read a record at the start.
findings.assumption: The rule (searched, not read at the start) is what the check needs; the words "audit trail" in setup.md are not.

findings.summary: The brief (one-pass, step 3 and "Permission ledger") says that the agent decides what the owner does not answer by an order of authority (the entry file wins over a page, a newer guide over an older one, a rule that only a record states is not in force), and that a ledger line names the owner's answer or that order. The shipped text has no order of authority: a conflict that the code cannot settle is a question (cleanup.md:109-111, 133-135), the ledger accepts only an owner's answer (187-190), and a rule that lives only in a log is stated in a guide (92-94). The brief sentence "a question about one hold does not retire the general rule behind it" also has no shipped sentence. Commit 83beff3 removed these. No check of spec 11 asks for them.
findings.assumption: The shipped rule is the stricter one for permissions, so it is taken as within the brief; the owner should say if the order of authority must come back, because it bears on "take more decisions on behalf of the user".

findings.summary: No test has the tag [AC:payload-words-not-up]; the untagged test "the shipped words are not more than at field-24" and tests/payload-budget.test.mjs cover the check. In this repository trace.mjs reports all eight criteria as untraced (exit 2), because the tests are in joycraft-prototype and the queue declares no check input; in the prototype test file the other seven criteria have tags.

Spec 11, "Not covered", names "A word target for an entry file". The shipped reference has one: "Aim for at most half of the current word count". The brief withdrew the ruling "no word target", so the text follows the brief and the spec line is out of date.
